transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I need to flag a critical discrepancy. The draft plan calls for all 26 students to test together in Room 201 with one proctor, but the state administration manual limits a testing room to 14 students. I've already prepared Room 201 for 14 students and Room 202 for 12 students to comply with that requirement. However, this updated room plan has not yet been entered into the district tracker, which is likely why the draft still shows the single-room setup.

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I also need to flag a critical issue with the calculator policy in the draft plan. The draft calls for graphing calculators to be available throughout the assessment, but when I reviewed the current state mathematics assessment manual this week, I found that calculators may only be used on section 2, and they must be four-function calculators — not graphing calculators. This means the draft plan is out of compliance in two ways: calculator type and testing sections where calculators are permitted.

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I also need to flag a critical issue with the technology setup in the draft plan. The draft calls for digital testing on school tablets, but my device test found that the 26 assigned tablets cannot run the required secure testing application, and we cannot obtain compatible devices before May 14. I contacted the assessment vendor, and they confirmed that paper booklets are authorized as an alternative. However, this result has not yet been added to the plan, so the draft still calls for digital testing on tablets that won't work.

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I also need to flag a critical issue with the storage and security requirements in the draft plan. The draft calls for completed materials to be stored in the general records cabinet, but my security review of the state testing agreement — which I completed this week — requires that completed assessment materials be sealed in tamper-evident envelopes and stored in a locked cabinet for exactly 30 calendar days. The draft plan does not meet either of these requirements: it specifies the general records cabinet rather than a locked cabinet, and it makes no mention of tamper-evident envelopes. I have not yet updated the storage field in the plan, which is likely why the draft still reflects the non-compliant storage arrangement.
